- When sentiment is high (≥0.7) and forecast shows a sharp upward move, reduce the forecast by 5–10% to avoid overreaction.  
- When sentiment is low (≤0.3) and forecast shows a sharp downward move, increase the forecast by 5–10% to avoid undershooting.  
- If recent price history shows strong mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 consecutive days of price decline), adjust forecast to be slightly above the recent low, not below.  
- If forecast shows a spike followed by a steep drop, reduce the peak value by 10–15% to account for overshoot.  
- When sentiment is volatile (alternating high/low), avoid extreme forecasts; use smoother, trend-following adjustments rather than sharp directional moves.  
- For 30-day forecasts, if the last 3–5 days show strong downward momentum, add a 2–3% upward bias to counteract mean reversion.  
- If sentiment is consistently positive but price is trending down, reduce forecast slope to avoid “sentiment-driven” overcorrection.
